stem: A beginner wants a graphical interface for inspecting Azure resources. Which tool fits?

choices.A: An ARM template
choices.B: Azure portal
choices.C: Azure CLI
choices.D: Azure PowerShell

explanations.A: A template describes a deployment rather than a graphical interface.
explanations.B: The portal is Azure's browser-based management interface.
explanations.C: The CLI is a command-line interface.
explanations.D: Azure PowerShell provides cmdlets.

stem: A user signs into the portal but sees no resources in the expected project. What should be checked first?

choices.A: The selected directory, subscription, filters, and access permissions
choices.B: Whether a pricing estimate was saved
choices.C: Whether every resource has been migrated to Azure Arc
choices.D: Whether the browser has deployed a new VM

explanations.A: These determine which resources are visible.
explanations.B: An estimate does not grant resource visibility.
explanations.C: Arc is not required to view native Azure resources.
explanations.D: Portal sign-in does not require VM deployment.

stem: What is a useful purpose of an Azure portal dashboard?

choices.A: Present selected resource information in one view
choices.B: Grant all viewers Owner permissions
choices.C: Prevent all resource deletion
choices.D: Replace a resource's deployment template

explanations.A: Dashboards support visual inspection and organization.
explanations.B: A dashboard does not grant resource permissions.
explanations.C: Locks and authorization govern deletion.
explanations.D: A dashboard is not infrastructure as code.

stem: A resource-management operation is made through the portal. Which statement about authorization is accurate?

choices.A: The portal ignores Policy assignments
choices.B: The operation still requires appropriate Azure permissions
choices.C: The portal can always delete locked resources
choices.D: Portal users automatically become subscription Owners

explanations.A: Applicable governance checks still matter.
explanations.B: A graphical interface does not bypass access checks.
explanations.C: Resource locks can block operations.
explanations.D: Sign-in does not create that grant.

stem: Which action is well suited to the portal for a first investigation?

choices.A: Bypass a deny policy by selecting a different menu
choices.B: Store a shared password in a dashboard tile
choices.C: Create every resource automatically on sign-in
choices.D: Inspect a resource's properties and available monitoring views

explanations.A: UI navigation does not bypass governance.
explanations.B: Credentials should not be placed in dashboards.
explanations.C: Signing in does not deploy all resources.
explanations.D: The visual interface can help explore a resource.

stem: A team needs the same environment recreated consistently across many runs. Which approach complements portal exploration?

choices.A: Repeat undocumented clicks from memory
choices.B: Assume the dashboard stores complete deployment logic
choices.C: Use reviewed scripts or declarative templates
choices.D: Give every user Owner so results match

explanations.A: That is harder to reproduce and review.
explanations.B: A dashboard is not a deployment specification.
explanations.C: Automation makes intended configuration repeatable.
explanations.D: Permissions do not ensure consistent configuration.

stem: Which Azure portal feature helps locate a service when its navigation position is unfamiliar?

choices.A: Search
choices.B: A VM availability set
choices.C: A resource lock
choices.D: A storage redundancy selector

explanations.A: The portal provides search for services and resources.
explanations.B: That affects compute placement.
explanations.C: That protects operations rather than finding services.
explanations.D: That configures storage resiliency.

stem: Why should a learner confirm the active subscription before a portal deployment?

choices.A: A subscription selection grants the caller Owner
choices.B: The chosen subscription determines the target resource and billing boundary
choices.C: Subscription scope matters only for command-line deployments
choices.D: A portal deployment always targets every accessible subscription

explanations.A: Target selection does not create a role assignment.
explanations.B: The wrong subscription can place resources in the wrong scope.
explanations.C: Portal operations also need the intended resource scope.
explanations.D: A deployment has a selected scope.

stem: What does successful navigation to a resource page prove?

choices.A: The resource has no chargeable components
choices.B: The user has enough visibility to open that page
choices.C: Every deployment command will succeed
choices.D: The user can remove every inherited lock

explanations.A: Visibility does not imply zero cost.
explanations.B: It does not prove permission for every possible action.
explanations.C: Other permissions, policies, and limits can still block changes.
explanations.D: Lock management needs suitable permissions.

stem: A learner compares a portal view with az resource list. Why might the displayed sets differ?

choices.A: The portal automatically duplicates resources
choices.B: They may use different subscription scopes or filters
choices.C: The portal and CLI necessarily use separate clouds
choices.D: The CLI never returns resource IDs

explanations.A: Viewing resources does not duplicate them.
explanations.B: Scope and filtering need to match before comparing.
explanations.C: They can address the same Azure environment.
explanations.D: Resource listings include IDs.

stem: What is Azure Cloud Shell?

choices.A: A new Azure resource hierarchy level
choices.B: A browser-accessible hosted shell with Azure management tools
choices.C: A storage redundancy model
choices.D: An Entra authentication-factor category

explanations.A: It is tooling rather than a hierarchy container.
explanations.B: It provides a managed command-line environment.
explanations.C: It is unrelated to data replication.
explanations.D: It is not a factor category.

stem: Which statement distinguishes a shell from the Azure CLI?

choices.A: PowerShell can host az commands; Azure CLI is the command tool being invoked
choices.B: Azure CLI can run only inside Bash
choices.C: Cloud Shell is the same product as an ARM template
choices.D: Every PowerShell command is an Azure PowerShell cmdlet

explanations.A: The shell and the command interface are different layers.
explanations.B: It can also run in PowerShell.
explanations.C: A shell hosts tools; a template describes infrastructure.
explanations.D: PowerShell can run other executables.

stem: Which command syntax belongs to Azure CLI?

choices.A: az group list
choices.B: Get-AzResourceGroup
choices.C: Connect-AzAccount
choices.D: Get-AzSubscription

explanations.A: The az executable uses command groups and subcommands.
explanations.B: That is an Azure PowerShell cmdlet.
explanations.C: That is an Azure PowerShell sign-in cmdlet.
explanations.D: That is an Azure PowerShell cmdlet.

stem: Which command syntax belongs to Azure PowerShell?

choices.A: Get-AzResourceGroup
choices.B: az resource list
choices.C: az account show
choices.D: az group list

explanations.A: Az-module cmdlets use PowerShell verb-noun names.
explanations.B: That is Azure CLI syntax.
explanations.C: That is Azure CLI syntax.
explanations.D: That is Azure CLI syntax.

stem: Why is Azure CLI output converted with ConvertFrom-Json in a PowerShell script?

choices.A: To grant the caller new Azure roles
choices.B: To work with the JSON result as PowerShell objects
choices.C: To deploy a VM from every output row
choices.D: To move resources to another region

explanations.A: Parsing does not change authorization.
explanations.B: Parsing supports property access and validation.
explanations.C: Conversion is a local data operation.
explanations.D: Parsing does not relocate resources.

stem: What is one benefit of CLI or PowerShell automation?

choices.A: Automation removes the need for error handling
choices.B: A sequence can be saved, reviewed, and repeated
choices.C: Scripts guarantee that every service is free
choices.D: Commands bypass all role assignments

explanations.A: Scripts must still handle failures.
explanations.B: Scripts preserve operations more explicitly than remembered interactions.
explanations.C: Costs depend on deployed services and usage.
explanations.D: Automation still needs authorization.

stem: A lab calls az resource list from PowerShell 7. Which tools are involved?

choices.A: Only the Azure portal
choices.B: Only a Bicep compiler
choices.C: Only the Azure PowerShell Az module
choices.D: The PowerShell shell and Azure CLI

explanations.A: This is a command-line operation.
explanations.B: No Bicep compilation is implied.
explanations.C: The az executable is a separate tool.
explanations.D: PowerShell hosts the az executable.

stem: A Cloud Shell session ends. What should a learner assume about resources created earlier?

choices.A: All billing ceases permanently
choices.B: Every created resource is automatically deleted
choices.C: All role assignments are removed
choices.D: Azure resources remain until appropriately stopped or deleted

explanations.A: Running resources can continue to incur charges.
explanations.B: Session lifetime and resource lifetime differ.
explanations.C: Closing the shell does not revoke assignments.
explanations.D: Ending a shell session is not resource cleanup.

stem: Which difference affects scripting between Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell?

choices.A: Azure PowerShell can manage only local files
choices.B: Azure CLI cannot be called from scripts
choices.C: CLI commonly returns JSON text; Az cmdlets return PowerShell objects
choices.D: One interface can authorize any user without roles

explanations.A: Its Az modules manage Azure resources.
explanations.B: It is commonly scripted.
explanations.C: Output handling differs between the interfaces.
explanations.D: Neither bypasses authorization.

stem: Why should a script pass an explicit subscription ID?

choices.A: It makes all resource operations free
choices.B: It guarantees that every provider is registered
choices.C: It supplies an authentication factor
choices.D: It makes the intended target independent of an ambiguous default context

explanations.A: Scope selection does not waive charges.
explanations.B: Provider availability must still be checked.
explanations.C: The subscription ID is an identifier, not a secret proof.
explanations.D: Explicit scope improves repeatability and safety.

stem: A company wants Azure governance visibility for servers that remain in its datacenter. Which service should it evaluate?

choices.A: Azure Migrate alone
choices.B: Azure App Service
choices.C: Azure Data Box
choices.D: Azure Arc

explanations.A: Migration tooling assesses and moves workloads rather than supplying this ongoing projection.
explanations.B: App Service hosts managed applications.
explanations.C: Data Box moves data offline.
explanations.D: Arc extends management to supported non-Azure infrastructure.

stem: What does connecting a supported external server to Azure Arc create?

choices.A: A guarantee of free monitoring ingestion
choices.B: An automatic replacement of the server's operating system
choices.C: An Azure resource representation for management
choices.D: A physical relocation of the server to an Azure datacenter

explanations.A: Connected services can have separate costs.
explanations.B: Onboarding does not imply OS replacement.
explanations.C: The server can be managed within Azure resource scopes.
explanations.D: Arc connection does not move the hardware.

stem: Which environments can be relevant to Azure Arc?

choices.A: On-premises, edge, and other-cloud environments
choices.B: Only Azure Storage blob accounts
choices.C: Only native Azure VMs in one subscription
choices.D: Only Microsoft 365 document identities

explanations.A: Arc addresses management beyond Azure datacenters.
explanations.B: Arc covers supported hybrid infrastructure rather than being a blob-only service.
explanations.C: Arc's distinguishing purpose includes supported resources outside Azure.
explanations.D: Arc is infrastructure management rather than an identity-provider configuration.

stem: A team needs to move a workload into Azure rather than manage it in place. Which distinction matters?

choices.A: Arc management and workload migration solve different needs
choices.B: Arc always migrates every connected workload
choices.C: Both terms mean the same action
choices.D: Migration only changes resource tags

explanations.A: Arc connection alone is not a migration.
explanations.B: It does not universally relocate workloads.
explanations.C: They describe different operational goals.
explanations.D: Migration can move workload data and hosting.

stem: What is a typical component for connecting a supported server to Azure Arc?

choices.A: The Azure Connected Machine agent
choices.B: A pricing calculator estimate
choices.C: A CanNotDelete lock on a glossary
choices.D: A storage archive access tier

explanations.A: The agent connects external server management to Azure.
explanations.B: An estimate does not install connectivity.
explanations.C: Locks are unrelated to server onboarding.
explanations.D: Tiering does not connect a server.

stem: Why should the organization review Arc extensions before enabling them?

choices.A: Every extension automatically moves the server to Azure
choices.B: They can add capabilities, permissions, and separate service charges
choices.C: All extensions are always free and require no authority
choices.D: Extensions replace the need for the server operating system

explanations.A: Extension activation is not universal migration.
explanations.B: Connected management still has operational and cost implications.
explanations.C: That is not a safe assumption.
explanations.D: They run alongside infrastructure rather than replacing it.

stem: Which governance advantage can an Arc resource representation provide?

choices.A: Remove all network connectivity prerequisites
choices.B: Move the connected machine's disks into Azure automatically
choices.C: Automatically transfer guest-OS patching to Microsoft for every external server
choices.D: Use Azure scopes and tags to organize supported hybrid resources

explanations.A: Connected management requires suitable communication.
explanations.B: Management representation does not imply data migration.
explanations.C: The customer still owns relevant external-infrastructure duties.
explanations.D: The representation integrates external infrastructure with Azure management.

stem: A connected external server stops communicating with Azure. What should an operator investigate?

choices.A: Agent status and required network connectivity
choices.B: Only whether the machine has a CostCenter tag
choices.C: Only whether a VM reservation was purchased
choices.D: Only whether the resource group has a delete lock

explanations.A: These affect management connection health.
explanations.B: An allocation tag alone does not diagnose agent connectivity.
explanations.C: A compute commitment does not restore an external agent connection.
explanations.D: Deletion protection does not by itself diagnose communication health.

stem: Why does this fundamentals lab avoid onboarding the learner's computer to Arc?

choices.A: Azure CLI can never inspect Arc resource types
choices.B: Arc requires no permissions, costs, or configuration
choices.C: Arc cannot manage any supported non-Azure servers
choices.D: Onboarding is an operational change beyond read-only tool comparison

explanations.A: Azure management tools can inspect relevant resources.
explanations.B: Requirements and connected-service costs need review.
explanations.C: That contradicts its purpose.
explanations.D: The concept can be learned without installing agents.

stem: Which statement about cost is appropriate for Arc-connected infrastructure?

choices.A: Arc converts every workload to a VM reservation
choices.B: Every connected service is permanently free
choices.C: Arc cancels all local datacenter costs
choices.D: Optional Azure services used with Arc can incur their own charges

explanations.A: Management projection does not impose that pricing model.
explanations.B: Service pricing still applies.
explanations.C: On-premises infrastructure remains the customer's expense.
explanations.D: Connection does not make every enabled service free.
